newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-New NZ cricketers may not play in India.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-New NZ cricketers may not play in India.

text.p: CHANDIGARH, May 7 - Rookie tourists Craig McMillan and Shayne O'Connor could be assigned a look, listen and learn brief on the New Zealand cricket team's brief tour of India.
There is no guarantee the two newcomers will be blooded during the Independence Cup quadrangular one-day tournament also featuring hosts India, World Cup holders Sri Lanka and Pakistan.
Coach Steve Rixon makes no apologies if Canterbury batsman McMillan and Otago left arm medium-fast bowler O'Connor return home without a game.
New Zealand play their first match in the tournament against Pakistan at PCA Stadium at Mohali, on the outskirts of Chandigarh on Friday.

"You blood people when you have got the time and the extra games to do so," Rixon told NZPA here yesterday after the Kiwis enjoyed a solid 2-1/2 hour training session at the stadium's superb practice facilities.
The compact nature of this tournament allows minimal experimentation for Rixon and his captain Stephen Fleming.
It is highly probable New Zealand will need to win two of their three preliminary matches to qualify for the best-of-three final.
"We have to pick our best team always," Rixon said.
"If the team play well in their first game then the same players will take the park for the second match.
"Craig and Shayne are basically here as alternatives if the original side do not weigh up."
If everything goes to plan, McMillan and O'Connor will find themselves observing the action from beyond the boundary's edge and familiarising themselves with touring life mostly in the nets.

McMillan, 20, forced his way into the national side by scoring a mountain of runs for Canterbury last summer when he set a new Shell Trophy benchmark for his province of 809 runs at an average 73 per innings.
In contrast, O'Connor finds himself in the squad because front-line seamer Simon Doull was forced out by injury.

O'Connor, a solidly built 1.94m bowler who possesses the sought after ability to swing the ball into right handed batsmen, had a profitable season for Otago, capturing 44 wickets in the Shell Trophy and Cup competitions.
Rixon said McMillan was considered as potential cover for any one of the six top batting slots despite playing primarily for Canterbury in the middle order.
"We would look to use him anywhere from one to six if someone gets injured or someone misses out.
"He has a good strike rate and if he and (Nathan) Astle opened together we'd be sure to get our early runs in a hurry."
